name: Seward
subtitle: Where a thousand stories begin.
alt: Boats and mountain scenery at Seward Small Boat Harbour
caption: Seward Small Boat Harbour, August 2025.
history: Seward became a winter port for the Iditarod gold fields, sending mail, supplies, and travelers inland. Today the waterfront marks Mile Zero of the National Historic Trail.

summer.label: Coastal discovery
summer.note: Begin with the waterfront and the trail's Mile Zero history. Allow time to explore the town, and check local access before setting out.

winter.label: A winter gateway
winter.note: Start with Seward's trail history. Snow, ice, and opening hours can change the day; check local conditions before a waterfront walk.

name: Crow Pass
subtitle: Follow history into the high country.
alt: Alpine landscape in Crow Pass Valley, Alaska
credit: National Park Service, Alaska Region / CC BY 2.0
caption: Crow Pass Valley, July 2017.
history: The Crow Pass trail follows part of the historic Iditarod corridor through the Chugach Mountains, connecting the Girdwood and Eagle River sides of the range.

summer.label: Summer hiking
summer.note: Plan with the official trail guide. Snow can linger; weather, river crossings, and the length of your chosen route require preparation.

winter.label: Plan for summer
winter.note: This is a summer hiking suggestion. Winter and spring avalanche exposure makes the pass unsuitable for a casual winter walk.
winter.link_label: Seasonal guidance from Alaska Fish & Game

name: Knik
subtitle: A townsite with a trail-sized story.
alt: A cabin at the historic Knik townsite, Alaska
caption: Historic Knik townsite cabin, September 2014.
history: Knik's history reaches beyond its gold-rush years. The community grew as an Upper Cook Inlet trading and supply center, connected to winter routes leading into the Interior.

summer.label: Heritage discovery
summer.note: Explore the story of the historic townsite. Confirm local access and seasonal opening hours before visiting heritage sites.

winter.label: Winter trail stories
winter.note: Discover the people and winter journeys connected with Knik. Historic routes cross different landowners; this map does not establish public access.

name: Iditarod
subtitle: A name carried far beyond a town.
alt: Historical photograph of First Street in Iditarod on July 20, 1910
credit: C. W. Felch / UW Libraries, Special Collections
caption: From the archive: First Street, July 20, 1910.
history: The Iditarod gold rush helped drive a network of winter supply routes into the Interior. This 1910 photograph captures the town during that early boom; it is not a view of the site today.

summer.label: Explore from the archive
summer.note: Explore this remote historic place through photographs and documents. This entry is an invitation to learn, not a suggested summer walking route.

winter.label: The winter supply trail
winter.note: Follow the stories of winter travel and supply. Any travel to this remote historic site requires independent planning and current local knowledge.

name: Unalakleet
subtitle: Where inland journeys meet the sea.
alt: Aerial photograph of Unalakleet village at the river mouth on Norton Sound
credit: Dr. John Cloud / NOAA Central Library
caption: Unalakleet village and river mouth, August 2010.
history: Unalakleet has long connected coastal communities with the Yukon River through the Kaltag Portage. Its trading history is part of a living community story that predates the gold rush.

summer.label: Community & coast
summer.note: Begin with the community's story and seek local guidance for a visit. Respect private land, community spaces, and subsistence activities.

winter.label: A living winter connection
winter.note: Discover how winter travel connects the coast and Interior. The shoreline and river are not presented here as safe travel routes; seek current local advice.

name: Nome
subtitle: The journey becomes a legacy.
alt: Bering Sea shoreline at Nome, Alaska, with offshore sea ice
caption: Nome's Bering Sea shoreline, June 2006.
history: Nome is the northern gateway of the National Historic Trail. Its gold-rush history sits within a much longer story of Alaska Native life on the Seward Peninsula.

summer.label: Coast & cultural heritage
summer.note: Explore the city's heritage and Bering Sea setting. Check museum information and local guidance when planning time in town.

winter.label: Stories at the trail's end
winter.note: Explore the stories of Nome and winter travel through the museum and community resources. Confirm opening hours and current conditions locally.
